theme: 3 terms on handling optionals: safe access, default value and the risky shortcut

terms.definition: A way to read a property or call a method on an optional, and get nil if the optional is nil.
terms.example: Use optional chaining, so a missing `user` gives nil, not a crash.
terms.code:
let name: String? = "Mina"
print(name?.uppercased() as Any)

terms.definition: The `??` operator, which gives a default value when an optional is nil.
terms.example: Use the nil-coalescing operator, so a missing nickname becomes "Guest".

terms.definition: Using `!` to take the value out of an optional, which crashes if it is nil.
terms.example: Avoid force unwrapping here, because `user` can be nil and the app would crash.

quizzes.question: In this code, what is it called when `!` takes the value out and crashes if `nickname` is nil?
quizzes.code:
let nickname: String? = nil
let name = nickname!

quizzes.question: In this code, what is it called when `??` gives "Guest" if `nickname` is nil?
quizzes.code:
let nickname: String? = nil
let name = nickname ?? "Guest"

quizzes.question: In this code, what is it called when `?.` stops and gives nil if `user` is nil?

video.title: Optional Chaining, Nil-Coalescing Operator & Force Unwrapping | iOS Daily English Day 18
video.description:
Learn to talk about Swift optionals beyond binding: Optional Chaining, Nil-Coalescing Operator & Force Unwrapping, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Optional Chaining - A way to read a property or call a method on an optional, and get nil if the optional is nil.
Nil-Coalescing Operator - The `??` operator, which gives a default value when an optional is nil.
Force Unwrapping - Using `!` to take the value out of an optional, which crashes if it is nil.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

dialogue.title: The safe nickname

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Mina, `user` can be nil. How do I read the nickname safely?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So optional chaining just returns nil if `user` is nil?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. The result is optional too.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I want "Guest" when it is nil.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then add the nil-coalescing operator, like `user?.nickname ?? "Guest"`.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Nice. Can I write `user!.nickname` instead? It is shorter.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No, that is force unwrapping. It crashes when `user` is nil.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Oh, so force unwrapping is risky.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. The nil-coalescing operator is much safer.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Got it. I will use optional chaining first.
Use optional chaining, so a missing `user` gives nil.
